sections.title: The organization behind the software
sections.introMarkdown: Carson’s Crusaders Foundation supports children and families affected by pediatric cancer. Established in memory of Carson Richardson, its work includes help with treatment-related travel and support for siblings.

cards.title: Helping families get to treatment
cards.markdown: CCF provides gas cards, parking vouchers, and other transportation assistance through affiliated hospitals. Medical professionals apply on behalf of families.
cards.footerMarkdown:
**The dashboard’s role:** connect a family’s record with the assistance awarded, including the type, amount, card reference, and notes.

[CCF’s transportation program ↗](https://carsonscrusadersfoundation.org/our-transportation-program/)

cards.title: Making room for brothers and sisters
cards.markdown: CCF hosts events where siblings can enjoy time together and meet children in similar circumstances. Its birthday program also recognizes siblings with gifts.
cards.footerMarkdown:
**The dashboard’s role:** keep sibling information with the family and organize event registrations and attendee details.

[CCF’s sibling support program ↗](https://carsonscrusadersfoundation.org/our-sibling-support-program/)

blocks.markdown: The foundation also promotes childhood cancer awareness. This project focused on its operational records: families, assistance awards, and events. Learn more about CCF’s history and wider work on [the foundation’s website](https://carsonscrusadersfoundation.org/).

sections.title: What the team can do
sections.introMarkdown: The dashboard follows CCF’s existing work: find the family, record the assistance, or organize participation in an event.

blocks.caption: Dashboard capabilities and their practical purpose
rows: Find a family’s record
Patient lookup and linked parent, sibling, contact, and treatment-facility information.
The team can see the context for assistance and event participation together.
Record an assistance award
Benefit type, amount, the last six card digits, and notes linked to the recipient.
A team member can see what was recorded for that family and identify the card involved.
Review family participation
Benefits, siblings, and event registrations on the family detail page.
Related records can be reviewed from the same place.
Prepare an event
Event name, location, year, registration cutoff, and active status.
Staff can maintain event information through the dashboard.
Organize attendance
Registrations with attendees, adult counts, shirt sizes, and emergency contacts; a filterable attendee list.
Event preparation has the practical details needed for the people attending.

steps.title: Find the family
steps.markdown: Open the patient’s record and review the assistance already listed.

steps.title: Enter the award
steps.markdown: Choose its type, enter the amount and card reference, and add any notes.

steps.title: Keep it connected
steps.markdown: Save the benefit to the recipient’s record, alongside their existing assistance.

blocks.markdown: **Result:** the team has a record of the award and who received it.

steps.title: Set up the event
steps.markdown: Enter the name, location, year, and registration cutoff.

steps.title: Record participation
steps.markdown: Link a family’s registration to the event; include attendee information and emergency contacts.

steps.title: Review the attendee list
steps.markdown: Use the event detail page to view, sort, and filter the people attending.

blocks.markdown: **Result:** event details and family participation can be managed in the same application.
### Maintain a choice used by a form

steps.title: Identify the lookup
steps.markdown: For example, a treatment-facility choice is loaded from the database.

steps.title: Use the trained support process
steps.markdown: A designated CCF member maintains the corresponding MySQL lookup through the existing database structure.

steps.title: Check the form
steps.markdown: Confirm that the updated choice is available when the application loads the list.

blocks.markdown: **Result:** routine lookup maintenance can happen without changing and redeploying application code.

sections.title: Built with the people who use it
sections.introMarkdown: CCF members drove the product’s requirements. Several meetings and demonstrations at CCF meetings shaped a focused build around their direct requests.

steps.title: Start with the work
steps.markdown: CCF members described the records and tasks they needed help managing.

steps.title: Build for those tasks
steps.markdown: The application used familiar concepts: families, benefits, siblings, and events.

steps.title: Put it in front of CCF
steps.markdown: Demonstrations gave members a concrete application to respond to and guide.

steps.title: Plan for continued use
steps.markdown: A CCF member received training for database-led support after delivery.

cards.title: A constrained, pro bono build
cards.markdown: The software was provided free of charge. A tightly constrained build made the team’s requests the basis for deciding what to include.

cards.title: Familiar concepts carried through
cards.markdown: The screens and underlying records mirror the organization’s activities. A CCF member could learn how those records fit together when supporting the system.

sections.title: Designed to be supported by CCF
sections.introMarkdown: The support plan was part of the design: routine upkeep should primarily involve a trained member working with MySQL, rather than requiring application code changes each time.

nodes.title: Use the dashboard
nodes.markdown: Manage family details, record assistance, and maintain events and registrations.

nodes.title: MySQL
nodes.markdown: Store the operational data and provide lookup choices and stored procedures used by the application.

nodes.title: A designated CCF member
nodes.markdown: Handle routine database support using an understandable record structure and the training provided.

blocks.markdown: A support model, not a database access guide. Application features still need code changes when the workflow itself changes.

blocks.caption: Support needs and where they are handled
rows: A new award or registration
Normal work in the dashboard, linked to the relevant family or event.
A routine lookup update
The existing MySQL lookup structure, maintained by a trained member. Forms load choices through database procedures.
A new workflow or screen
An application change. Database-led support was intended to reduce routine code work, not replace development entirely.

blocks.markdown: The application uses C# and ASP.NET Core MVC with MySQL and stored procedures. The important design choice for this project was keeping its records and maintenance understandable to the team who would own it.

sections.title: Several years of everyday use
sections.introMarkdown: The dashboard remains in active production use and has helped CCF manage its operations for multiple years.
